newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by weak pork demand, dealers said.
The weak pork demand kept packer buying interest light as margins remained in unprofitable territory, they said.
Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $53.00 to $53.50 and Illinois top prices could range $52.50 to $53.00.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range $52.00 to $52.50, the dealers said.

Fresh pork prices near midday were not well tested, but had a weak tone, butts were firm to $ 1.00 per cwt higher, hams were steady, bellies steady to $1.00 lower and lean trimmings steady to $1.50 lower, USDA said.
Sluggish pork demand and poor margins spurred at least one major packer to reduce operations.

John Morrell and Co.'s hog plant in Sioux City, Iowa, dropped its second shift on Monday for an undetermined length of time, company sources said. The Sioux City plant has a daily estimated capacity up 16,000 head, market sources said.
